messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

decision.detail: Set the telegram down on the desk, face-up, where whoever's next can read it. Coil the last of the cable, tuck it into the case, click the latches. Set the case on the shelf by the door where it goes. Unhook the strap from my shoulder. The lights outside are still up, the whole festival rig glowing pink and gold through the window, and I can hear the old projectionist's voice from the lobby, mid-sentence, wanting to tell me about a 1947 reel of *The Magnificent Ambersons* he kept in a closet in Dayton. I don't go out to him. No charge. No second take. I just nod at the glass, once, and turn the key in the lock behind me.
decision.intention: Go home. The reel is the patch's now. The daughter in Pittsburgh got it and wants it back—that's the job working, that's the whole job. I don't need a copy. I don't need to sit in the booth and listen to Alma's voice a second time, hear the charge flatten out mid-word again. I'll walk to the corner store, maybe buy a bottle of something, maybe just stand in the doorway and look at the festival lights from the sidewalk because they're on and I'm standing here and it's free. Then I'll go to the Rialto's back lot, sit on the cooler, and wait for it to get dark. It'll be dark by morning. That's how it is.

2. go_off_duty: Put the kit away and go off duty.

My internal state: "I just needed one good angle of a woman talking to her daughter and the charge dying in the middle of a sentence. I got it. Now I go home."

I don't need to keep a copy for myself - it's not mine anymore, it's the patch's. I don't need to listen to it again - I already heard it, I already got my angle, the charge died mid-sentence and that's the shot. I've already made peace with it: "That's how it is."

The lights are on. The projectionist wants to talk. But I've got no charge. I can't shoot. And I don't need to. I'll put the kit away and go. Maybe I'll drink a beer in the lobby. Maybe I won't. The Rialto will be dark by morning.

Let me pick: go_off_duty.

Physical act: Put the kit away. Coil the cable, close the case, set it on the shelf by the door.

Words: Maybe I say something to whoever's at the station. Or maybe I don't. The prompt says "Silence is allowed." I think a small acknowledgment of the telegram is appropriate - I read it, I nod. "She got it. Good." That's it. Not performative. Just acknowledging.

Practical intention: Go home. The reel belongs to the patch now. The lights will be there in the morning or they won't, and it doesn't change what I shot. I'll walk out, maybe grab a beer, maybe not. The Rialto will be dark by morning.

Let me write this as Larry. First person, physical, grounded. Not overwrought. A camera operator who's done his one take and is putting the kit away.
